Phlebotomists play critical roles in hospitals, clinics, testing labs, and blood donation centers. They help physicians correctly detect diseases by providing blood samples from patients. Other phlebotomist roles and responsibilities include:
Explaining to the patient why blood is being drawn 
Determining a patient's tolerance for venipuncture, or the procedure of puncturing a vein to withdraw blood
Assisting individuals in becoming comfortable throughout the procedure
Basic vitals such as blood sugar and blood pressure readings
Keeping medical supplies and equipment under their control
